Medical/coding evaluations and initialization profiling directly test broader applicability and practical efficiency, while interpretations become better qualified. Single-run evidence still limits confidence, and Algorithm 1 introduces a scaling inconsistency, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains.

The novelty, analyzability, plug-and-play, and compression contributions remain unchanged; logical-reasoning coverage was already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: New discussion interprets the shared-backbone results as evidence against a pretraining-only explanation and argues that inference savings offset training overhead. Appendix G strengthens the termination explanation into an asserted intrinsic continuous-space difficulty, without a new causal test. Existing limitations and case interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: v3 adds homepage and model-collection access links and documents hardware, epoch allocation, and measured costs for the training-time comparison. Original implementation hyperparameters remain unchanged. The new GPQA/ProsQA evaluation receives only a general statement that implementation details are consistent with the existing setup.

E2.justification: The original comparator sets remain intact. New Tables 8-9 reuse Coconut, CODI, and CoLaR-2, already evaluated in v1. The documented differences concern backbone settings and task coverage; no comparator-algorithm revision is specified.

E3.justification: Appendix E adds a controlled comparison placing RoT and three baselines on Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct, addressing the differing backbones in retained Table 2. Appendix D introduces training-time measurements with matched three-epoch budgets, batch size 16, and one H20 GPU. Existing experimental protocols are retained.

Existing stage, projection-head, rendering, decoding, and case analyses remain unchanged. Appendix G adds discussion, not another termination experiment.

E5.justification: The five-seed/95% confidence-interval statement and existing uncertainty entries remain unchanged. New appendix tables report point values, as earlier appendix ablation tables already did; no changed run counts or statistical estimation procedures are specified.

E6.justification: Tables 7-9 add training times of 56.1 hours for RoT versus 36.9 for SFT-CoT, VLM-based comparator results including CoLaR-2's 45.3 average versus RoT's retained 55.4, and RoT Pass@1 scores of 60.5 on GPQA and 100.0 on ProsQA. Original Tables 1-6 and plotted findings are unchanged. The new backbone results are additional evaluations, not corrections or same-setting performance changes.

P1.justification: Changes include limited abstract/introduction wording, author-order and affiliation edits, and four new appendix sections with an expanded contents list. The case study becomes Appendix H, with updated cross-references. The existing narrative is largely retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds three compact appendix tables and a title-page resource strip. Figure 2 moves earlier, some tables become more compact, and appendix material shifts. Original figure content and existing table structures remain intact.

R1.justification: v3 adds the GPQA reference by Rein et al. and expands discussion connecting termination difficulties to the already cited LVR work. The related-work section and central novelty positioning otherwise remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The loss equations, termination definition, and special-token normalization remain unchanged. Appendix G's continuous-space explanation introduces no formal assumption, theorem, derivation, or proof.

results.title: Render-of-Thought: Rendering Textual Chain-of-Thought as Images for Visual Latent Reasoning

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion replace the attribution of hard-negative gains to superior LLM understanding of negation with an explanation emphasizing audio-space separation and word-order sensitivity shared with CLAP. This substantially revises a central explanatory claim while retaining the headline retrieval-performance claims.

C2.justification: V3 rejects the earlier contrast between compositional OEA processing and bag-of-content CLAP processing: its controls find exclusion-sensitive word-order effects in every tested encoder. It also explains that exclusion clauses attract excluded content rather than cleanly suppressing it, clarifies sample-based validation limits and recasts comparison with real search-query distributions as future work.

D1.justification: V3 adds encoder and deployment details, including audio-encoder dimensions, bidirectional attention and inactive speech-generation components, plus implementation details for the new controls. It revises dataset-release and access statements and removes annotator recruitment/payment details. Core training hyperparameters and generation prompts are retained.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation datasets remain unchanged. Appendix O extends testing to word-order-corrupted queries and matched queries with exclusion clauses removed, adding controlled input scenarios within the existing AudioCaps, Clotho and MECAT coverage.

E2.justification: The original benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged. Appendix O.3 newly evaluates a pre-transformer mean-pooling control, reporting R@1 approximately zero, while the new mechanism comparisons reuse M2D-CLAP, MGA-CLAP and LAION-CLAP.

E3.justification: Appendix O introduces fixed-checkpoint diagnostic protocols on 630 AudioCaps, 542 Clotho and 409 MECAT pairs: audio-only separation, matched exclusion-clause removal and identical word shuffles across encoders. Benchmark-curation descriptions also change from sampled rejection/regeneration to post-hoc query validation and human-guided threshold calibration. These are reported protocol revisions, without evidence that the original benchmark experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2's proposed explanation for hard-negative gains was largely interpretive. V3 adds a substantial mechanism-analysis suite separating audio geometry, exclusion-clause effects and word-order sensitivity, including cross-model shuffle controls that challenge the earlier explanation.

E5.justification: V3 adds paired Wilcoxon signed-rank testing for audio separation and shuffle effects, including dataset-specific significance and comparisons of exclusion-specific structure contributions. This substantially extends inferential reporting beyond the retained human/LLM validation statistics. No repeated-training-run or multi-seed evaluation is introduced.

E6.justification: The original retrieval tables retain their values. New Tables 17–20 report diagnostic outcomes, including mean audio distances of 0.317 versus 0.223 for OEA and M2D-CLAP, deterioration when exclusion clauses are present, and OEA exclusionary Δ-Rank falling from 22.5 to -7.2 after shuffling. These are newly reported diagnostic results, not improvements over v2 under established identical settings.

M1.justification: The shared backbone, LoRA adapters, projection heads, pooling and contrastive objective remain unchanged. Appendix O explicitly evaluates a released checkpoint without retraining; the revised human-curation descriptions concern benchmark construction and validation.

P1.justification: The explanatory narrative and appendix organization are substantially revised. Section 5.4 is absorbed into appendix discussions, Appendices H–M are reordered, the query-distribution discussion becomes a bias analysis, and the conclusion, limitations, efficiency and scaling discussions are rewritten.

P2.justification: Figure 2 corrects the second training input from 'Text Batch' to 'Audio Batch'; Figures 1 and 3 are unchanged. Four diagnostic tables are added, duplicate efficiency displays are consolidated into a compact appendix table, and several tables are reformatted or relocated. The overall visual design remains stable.

R1.justification: V3 adds Wang et al. (2024), the E5 embedding work, and invokes E5/BGE literature to contextualize retrieval scaling. The main related-work sections and other cited works remain, while the claimed distinction from CLAP text processing is narrowed.

T1.justification: Appendix O introduces mathematical diagnostic contrasts, including ΔΔ-Rank for clause effects and S(m), the exclusionary shuffle gap minus the positive-query shuffle gap. The original loss and retrieval-metric definitions remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

improvement.justification: V3 addresses an important weakness: v2 inferred specialized negation understanding from retrieval advantages without directly testing that explanation. Appendix O supplies controlled evidence that challenges this account, and the abstract and conclusion adopt a more qualified mechanism claim. Validation descriptions also become more explicit. New reporting defects remain—Table 19's positive-query gap disagrees with its displayed values, and Appendix L mislabels a human–LLM correlation as inter-annotator agreement—but these local inconsistencies do not outweigh the substantial improvement in testing and qualifying the central explanation.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Omni-Embed-Audio research. All 18 pages of v2 and 19 pages of v3, including their appendices, are readable and support matching text, equations, figures and tables.

after.justification: V3 retains these empirical results and adds audio-separation, negation-removal and query-shuffling experiments in Appendix O.

before.justification: V2 reports original retrieval experiments, human and LLM query validation, dataset-overlap analysis and inference-efficiency measurements.
